claims.claim: Defines "education," "education requirement," and "executive agency"
claims.sourceSpan: Definitions.--In this section

claims.claim: "Education" means an associate, baccalaureate, graduate, or professional degree, specified coursework, or other form of educational attainment awarded by a junior/community college, college, or university accredited as a collegiate institution by a recognized accrediting agency
claims.sourceSpan: an associate, baccalaureate, graduate, or professional degree, specified coursework, or other form of educational attainment awarded by a junior or community college, college, or university that is accredited as a collegiate institution by a recognized accrediting agency

claims.claim: Education may also be approved by the appropriate state education authority, or DC’s equivalent, to grant associate or higher degrees
claims.sourceSpan: approved by the appropriate State education authority under State law (or the appropriate education authority of the District of Columbia) to grant associate or higher degrees

claims.claim: "Education requirement" includes a requirement that can be met through education alone; education or experience; or a combination of education and experience
claims.sourceSpan: (A) education alone; (B) education or experience; or (C) a combination of education and experience

claims.sourceSpan: the meaning given that term in section 133 of title 41, United States Code

claims.note: Accurate gap: 2(g)(2) uses "experience" but 2(g) supplies no definition of it.

claims.claim: The bill requires a written justification in each solicitation but does not require the justification to be made public or reviewable by prospective bidders
claims.sourceSpan: includes in the solicitation a written justification
claims.note: Analytical over-reach: the justification is required IN the solicitation, which prospective bidders receive, so the "not reviewable by prospective bidders" characterization runs against the text; the broader "made public" point is an unstated inference. Non-material style debt, not a core-content error.

claims.claim: The bill requires OMB guidance to encourage alternatives to education requirements but does not name the alternatives (e.g., competency assessments, skills tests, portfolio review)

claims.note: Accurate gap: source encourages "alternatives" without naming any; the examples are the analyst’s illustration (flagged as e.g.).

claims.claim: The bill repeals Section 813 of the FY2001 NDAA but does not identify what happens to solicitations already using the current FAR subpart 39.104 flexibility framework during the 15-month applicability lag
